band.unit: ea (one complete PV grid-connection switchboard package, one building)
band.basis: Sum of the 15 components above: QV CostBuilder rows (unreviewed) for the isolating switches, PV board proxy, RCBO proxy, cable, tray and revenue meter; two fetched vendor pages for the 63A MCCB (ECS NZ) and the export-limit device (Fronius smart meter); and named allowances for relabelling/make-safe, unmeasured modification of the existing 400A board, CT/interface sundries, the penal-rate shutdown and certification/paperwork. Excludes GST, preliminaries, margin, design/consent fees and all network and meter-rental charges. Allowances carry about 36% of the high end, so confidence is low. Nominal quantity is one package, so $/ea equals the total: $6,200-$9,600 (mid about $7,900).

One complete PV grid-connection package for one building, serving one existing 400A TP&N main switchboard. Sum of the 13 components above: $7,531 low / $11,590 high, rounded to $7,530-$11,590. Nominal quantity is one package, so $/ea equals the total. Main cost drivers - electrician labour (QV row), the new PV board (QV row), the 4-pole Type B RCBO (QV proxy) and the meter (QV row) - are all sourced, so the band is established. Allowances carry about 18% of the low total and 26% of the high total, under a third. Confidence is low: QV publishes no PV, MCCB, Type B RCBO, export-relay or revenue-metering rows, so four devices are QV proxies with stated adjustments and the export-limit relay/CT hardware is an allowance. GST exclusive; excludes preliminaries, margin, design and consent fees, network and connection charges, meter rental, the inverter and all DC/array-side work, main switchboard replacement, asbestos/remediation, trenching, penetrations, scaffolding and EWP hire.

band.unit: ea (one complete PV grid-connection switchboard package for one building)
band.basis: Sum of the fourteen distinct components above (component totals 6,780 low / 10,240 high; mid-point 8,510), GST exclusive, no preliminaries and no margin. Nominal quantity is ONE package, so the amortisation is the whole figure: $6,800 - $10,200 for the one package and $/ea is identical. Main cost drivers are all sourced: the 12-way board enclosure, the electrician hourly rate (Auckland $83.65/h) and the export meter from QV CostBuilder rows (unreviewed, caveated), and the 63A 4-pole MCCB ($336.39) and 63A 4-pole IP66 AC isolator ($103.69) from fetched Tropac NZ pages. Allowances (Type B RCBO, zero-export relay/CTs, glands and sundries, relabelling, and the certification/documentation item) carry 22% of the low total and 33% of the high total, just under the one-third threshold, so confidence is medium rather than low. Low end assumes the new MCCB and main switch go into the existing board's spare ways without modification, mid-week shutdown in a normal window, and 16 hours of electrician time; high end assumes a busbar/chassis adaptation within the existing board, a weekend shutdown at 2.0x, 24 hours of electrician time, and a certified export meter and standalone export-limit relay. Excluded and NOT priced: GST, preliminaries, margin, design fees and consent fees; Vector/network application and connection charges and any meter rental; the 30 kW inverter, PV modules, mounting, DC cabling, DC isolators and all array-side work; replacement or upgrade of the existing main switchboard and any asbestos or switchboard-remediation work; trenching, building fabric penetrations, scaffolding or EWP hire; monitoring platform subscriptions, data logger SIM or comms cabling beyond 5 m. No contingency is included: if the 15-year-old 400A board will not accept the new switchgear in the spare ways, that is a variation and should be preceded by a board inspection.

band.unit: $/ea (one complete PV grid-connection switchboard package for one building)
band.basis: Sum of the priced components above, Auckland, NZD, GST-exclusive, excluding preliminaries, margin, design fees and consent fees. Nominal quantity is ONE package, so $/ea equals the total: $6,918 low - $12,612 high (mid ~$9,765) for the one package; the amortisation is therefore fully auditable (nothing is divided down). Main cost drivers are all cited: the new PV board (QV t2:r8 proxy, $920-1,800), the revenue meter (QV t29:r5, $1,000-1,600) and the Type B RCBO (QV t29:r45 proxy, $760-1,600). QV electrical rows are installed rates, so no separate general installation-labour line has been added on top of them; only work no material row covers (commissioning, live-side make-safe, testing/paperwork, certification) is added. Labelled allowances total ~$1,600-3,750, i.e. about 23-30% of the band, which is under a third. Confidence is low because the two largest hardware lines rest on QV proxies for different products (a 15-way surface board for a 12-way TP&N IP44 board; a 3-pole 30mA RCD for a 4-pole Type B RCBO) and the zero-export device rests on a single Australian consumer-article figure; NZ wholesalers publish no price for it. The band is therefore a cost-plan range, not a certified price.
